newsitem.title: USA: Allegheny sees weak Q4 steel pricing.
newsitem.headline: Allegheny sees weak Q4 steel pricing.

text.p: The currently weak pricing environment in the stainless steel flat-rolled market will probably not improve in the fourth quarter, as some industry analysts had been predicting, said Arthur Aronson, executive vice president of Allegheny Teledyne Inc.

"I have no reason to think (pricing) will be any different (in the fourth quarter) than it was in the third quarter," Aronson told reporters at an investment forum in Pittsburgh on Thursday sponsored by Emerald Asset Management Inc.

Allegheny Teledyne, the largest U.S. producer of stainless flat-rolled products, and its competitors earlier this year withdrew a second-quarter price hike due to a heavy level of imports that were putting downward pressure on U.S. tags.
Some industry analysts had predicted that U.S. producers may have a shot at raising prices in the fourth quarter, but Aronson said pricing will remain weak through the end of the year.
Prices for stainless steel sheet Type 304, a bellwether grade, have fallen more than 20 percent since January. Domestic prices have been weakened by imports.
Weak prices in Europe and Asia attracted imports from those regions to the more lucrative U.S. market.

Aronson said, however, that some European producers recently raised prices. "(That's) a good sign," he said. "I think that there's at least some hope that we'll see some rationalization of the prices but I can't predict it. All I can do is hope."
Separtely, Aronson said Allegheny Teledyne has no plans to sell any businesses but the company would like to sell a steel bar plant in Owensboro, Kentucky.
That plant produces only carbon steel bar, which is not part of the company's core business of stainless and specialty metal products.
"It's an asset that we would like to sell," he said. "It's not a core business to us. It's not dragging our earnings down at all, it's accretive.
"But the fact of the matter is, we would like to sell it but we're not going to give it away." He declined to comment on a price the company would sell the plant for.
